decisions.q1_discovery_mechanism: RESOLVED-by-reality: no runtime discovery needed. Each provider self-discovers its OWN deployed file natively (Claude -> ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, OpenCode -> ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md, Copilot -> ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md, AGY -> $GEMINI_HOME/AGY.md). A binary-name->provider detector would have ZERO callers. REJECTED (YAGNI).
decisions.q2_backwards_compat: RESOLVED: never at risk - the slim-pointer CLAUDE.md already ships and is deploy-verified. No cutover required.
decisions.q3_colocation_vs_global: RESOLVED: per-repo overlays = ai/<provider>/ (co-located, git-synced); a global registry was the Layer-3 proposal, REJECTED below.
decisions.q4_state_md_format: OUT OF SCOPE: STATE.md cross-session handoff is MEMORY-001 territory, not the instruction boundary IDEAS-007 fixes.
decisions.q5_minimal_viable_subset: RESOLVED: the MVS already lives in AGENTS.md (identity, decision hierarchy, security halts, response protocol + the rest). Audit confirms no provider-specific rule leaked into it.
decisions.r2_telemetry: Path (c) qualitative audit adopted (this artifact). fires_observed annotated from session review, no instrumentation cost. Path (a) telemetry NOT triggered - the split is already validated as correct, so there is nothing to instrument-then-refactor.

rejected_yagni.layer_3_registry: ~/.config/agent-harness/providers/*.yaml - no runtime consumer; each provider's native config discovery already does the job.
rejected_yagni.discovery_mechanism: runtime binary-name->provider detector + bats - no caller. Building it would be dead code (Decision Hierarchy: Explicit > Implicit; boring tech).
rejected_yagni.rename_ai_to_dotagent: renaming ai/<provider>/ -> .agent/<id>/INSTRUCT.md - pure churn on a deployed convention wired into setup-linux.sh (~6 sites) + healthcheck; zero functional gain.

deferred_followup.summary: setup-linux.sh has ~5 near-identical per-provider deploy blocks (copy file -> grep-verify pointer). A data-driven manifest (provider|src|dst|verify-string) looped once would collapse ~80-100 LOC to ~30 + a manifest, making 'add a provider' a one-line change. This is the ONE genuine scalability win in IDEAS-007, but it is a setup-linux.sh refactor (different logical change), so it must be its own spec - NOT bundled here (Atomic PRs).
deferred_followup.trigger: do it when the 6th provider is added OR when the per-provider deploy blocks drift out of sync; YAGNI until then (5 providers, stable).
deferred_followup.also_subsumes: the stale claude-opus-4-7 model id could be fixed under the same manifest if model tiers move into it.
